name: Photocopy
summary: An office copier makes a print with toner on plain paper from a paste-up, with no plate and no press.
how: Paste up the page from typed text, hand lettering and cut pictures on one sheet.
Copy the paste-up; copy the copy to push the contrast and to lose the mid-tones.
Accept the toner speckle, the black edges of the cut paper and the grey of the glass.
Fold and staple the copies by hand.

origin.note: Xerox sells the 914, the first automatic plain-paper office copier.

adoptions.via: Mark Perry copies the paste-ups of Sniffin' Glue on an office copier, and punk zines follow.
